reason: The stalk that carries the gynostegium (Apocynaceae). Stalk part of the gynostegium class FLOPO_0986051 fits it.
The corolla of the disc florets of an Asteraceae head. Corolla part of disk flower fits it.
The stalked base of the Carex perigynium. Stalk part of perigynium fits it.
The veins of the glume between its two keels. Nerve is the same as vein, so vascular bundle part of glume fits. The word is not used for other organs.

'Distal' is lost. The rule sends the cells to all cells of the leaf, but moss descriptions set distal cells against basal or alar cells. A rule to a leaf-apex or distal-part container would keep that meaning. PO_0025606 (native plant cell) is also not the plant cell (PO_0009002) used by the sibling rules.
Cells of the moss operculum. Cell part of the operculum fits. Plant cell (PO_0009002) would match the sibling rules better than native plant cell.
The cells of the sheathing leaf base in mosses. Cell part of leaf base (PO_0020040) fits. 'Lamina' is a redundant word.
The anther of a staminode. Anther part of staminode fits.
Hairs of the lemma are trichomes (hair is a synonym of trichome in PO). Trichome part of lemma fits.
A gland on the leaf blade. Secretory tissue portion part of leaf lamina fits.
The pappus of the disc florets. Pappus part of disk flower fits.
A tooth on the margin of a leaflet blade. Leaf lamina tooth part of leaflet fits. 'Margin' is implied by the tooth.
A vein of a bract. Vascular bundle part of bract fits.
Lamina cells at the leaf apex. Plant cell part of leaf apex keeps the position.
Hairs on the moss calyptra are trichomes. Trichome part of calyptra fits.

'Costa filament cell' is a cell of the filaments that grow on the costa surface (for example in Pottiaceae). It is not an ordinary cell of the costa. The rule loses 'filament'. Leave it unresolved or add a filament class.
The cells of the moss capsule wall (exothecium). Cell part of exothecium fits.
Cells of the costa of a moss leaf. Cell part of costa fits.
The apex of a stipule. Plant organ apex part of stipule fits.
Singular form of 'exothecial cells'. Cell part of exothecium fits.
The scales on a Fagaceae fruit cup are bracts of the cupule. Bract part of cupule fits. Scale has several meanings, but 'fruit cup scale' names the cupule.
A segment of the grass spikelet rachilla is an internode of it. Inflorescence axis internode part of spikelet rachilla fits.
A cell of the leaf. Plant cell part of leaf fits.

Seed coat cell descriptions (shape, sculpture, anticlinal walls) usually mean the epidermal cells. The rule forces the container to seed coat epidermis. It is wrong for cells of deeper layers (palisade, sclerenchyma). Keep it only when the text is about surface cells, or use seed coat as the container.
Cells of the bulb coat, which is the tunic. Plant cell part of tunic fits.

The middle lobe of the orchid labellum. Labellum lobe part of orchid labellum fits. The median position is lost, but the review of 'median lobe' accepts this when the organ is named. Lateral and median lobes of the same labellum will not be told apart.
The stalk of a gland. Stalk part of portion of secretory tissue fits.
A bract on a scape. A scape is a peduncle, so bract part of peduncle fits.
The key names the counted part (spines) and the whole (areole), so it is not the empty 'per X' fragment. Cactus spines are modified leaves. Spine leaf part of areole bud fits, with a count quality.
Hairs on a rhizome are trichomes. Trichome part of rhizome fits.
The lamina (flat blade) of a ray flower corolla is the corolla limb of the ray flower. Corolla limb part of ray flower fits.
